sentences.text:
And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Anurag Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned AGA for the State and Sri Durgesh Kumar Pathak, Advocate who has put in appearance on behalf of opposite party no. 2.
This Court vide order dated 12.11.2021 directed the parties to file compromise deed before the court below concerned and the court below was directed to verify the contents and parties of the compromise deed.
In the present case, the sections involved are 323, 406, 420, 504, 506 IPC.

In compliance of the aforesaid order, compromise deed was filed before the court below concerned and the court concerned vide report dated 8.12.2021 has verified the contents and parties of the compromise deed and submitted his report to the extent that the parties and contents of the compromise deed are genuine and they have entered into the compromise by free-will.

sentences.text: 1 Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 has submitted that the parties in dispute are not interested to pursue the criminal case.

The Apex Court in re: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343 has observed that even if the offence (s) in question is / are not compoundable within the scope of section 320 Cr.P.C. even then considering the facts and circumstances of the case in question the Constitutional Court may allow the parties to compound such offence(s) on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.
